post.summary:
Exchanges a username and password for a JWT bearer token. Every other endpoint requires
the token this returns, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

M2-A04 — exchanges a live refresh token for a new access/refresh pair. One-time use with rotation: the presented token is revoked in the same call that issues its replacement (`RefreshTokenService.RotateAsync`), so replaying it always fails. Why `[AllowAnonymous]`. The access token that would normallyauthenticate this caller may already be expired — that is the entire reason thisendpoint exists. The refresh token itself is the credential. Tenant binding (BR-TEN-002). Deliberately not re-derived from a JWTclaim — an expired access token authenticates nobody, so `HttpContext.User` herecarries no claims to read. Tenant context instead comes from the same`ITenantProvider` host-resolution path `Login` already uses (Host header /tenant.json), which is how `ApplicationDbContext` — and therefore which tenant's`RefreshTokens` table this call ever sees — was already resolved before thisaction runs. A token issued in tenant A is simply absent from tenant B's database;there is no cross-tenant row to find, so there is nothing to switch.

M2-A04 — revokes the presented refresh token. Revokes exactly that one token, not
every token belonging to the user: the request contract is "the refresh token to
revoke" (singular), matching one-session-per-device logout. A revoke-all/"sign out
everywhere" capability is a natural extension, left to whichever future task needs it
rather than assumed here.
            

Idempotent by design (Target Result 4 / the logout error-model row): revoking anunknown or already-revoked token still returns `204` — the response must neverleak whether a token was ever valid.

get.summary: M2-B02 — the reference implementation of the paged list contract (ADR-002 §2 and its M2-B02 addendum). Every future list endpoint copies this shape: one `[FromQuery]` typed query record in, one V.SMART.Api.Contracts.PagedResult`1 out, the service's filter dictionary produced by V.SMART.Api.Contracts.FilterDictionaryAdapter and never seen on the wire. The controller-local paged-response record it replaces is deleted: 60–80copies of it would become 60–80 interfaces in the generated TypeScript client. TheJSON is unchanged — the four property names were already ADR-002's. Behaviour change to note: the default `pageSize` is now thecontract-wide 20, where this endpoint alone previously defaulted to 10. Callers thatsend `pageSize` explicitly are unaffected. Validation is declarative on V.SMART.Api.Contracts.CurrencyQuery, so an invalid`pageNumber`/`pageSize`/`sort`/date range is rejected by M2-A06's`InvalidModelStateResponseFactory` before this method runs. The explicit`ModelState` guard below is the belt-and-braces path for a caller that invokes theaction directly (unit tests), and matches `Create`/`Update`.

get.description: It does not call `DownloadTemplate(uploadType)`: that method's `LoadHeadings` switch knows four item-oriented upload types only (`ExcelTemplateService.cs:46-76`) and returns an empty header array for anything else, so a "Currency" upload type would silently produce an empty template. Passing the headers explicitly wraps the same service without modifying it.

post.summary: POST api/v1/currencies/import — `multipart/form-data` with `file`. Every row goes through `ICurrencyService.CreateAsync`. The controller parses the spreadsheet and does nothing else: duplicate detection, validation and persistence stay in the business service, and its refusal message is reported verbatim (BR-SO-001). A bad row is reported, not thrown; the remaining rows are still processed.

POST api/v1/files — `multipart/form-data` with `file`, `refType` and `docType`. The order of the checks is the security contract: extension allow-list, then size, then the duplicate-name business rule, and only then is a byte written. The stored record mirrors what `CorrespondenceUpload.razor:299-312` writes — file name, size string, content type, uploader, and the bytes in `Correspondence.Image` (`:306-309`) — so a file uploaded here is readable by the existing Blazor list screens. Two size limits, deliberately. The framework refuses anything over V.SMART.Api.Services.FileStorageOptions.DefaultMaxUploadBytes (20 MB) before the action runs — that attribute must be a compile-time constant — and the action then applies the configured `FileStorage:MaxUploadBytes`, which a deployment may lower. 20 MB is the same ceiling `WebFileUploadService.cs:101` passes to `OpenReadStream`. Note that the correspondence screen refuses at 5 MB (`CorrespondenceUpload.razor:222`) — a page-level rule, not a storage rule, and not carried here; a deployment wanting parity sets `FileStorage:MaxUploadBytes`.

get.summary: GET api/v1/files/{id} — the bytes, with the content type this API resolved from the file's extension and a `Content-Disposition: attachment` naming it. The SPA turns the response into a blob URL, exactly as ADR-005 specifies for PDFs. Why the database column is preferred over the file on disk. The bytes are held twice: on disk, and in `Correspondence.Image` (`Correspondence.cs:14`, written by `CorrespondenceUpload.razor:306-309`). For files uploaded through Blazor the two disagree — the on-disk copy is zero bytes because `WebFileUploadService.cs:102` is commented out — and the two live download screens disagree with each other about which to use: `CorrespondenceListByReference.razor:357-363` abandoned the path and serves the column, while `CorrespondanceList.razor:319-321` still opens the (empty) path. This endpoint follows the screen that works. The disk copy is the fallback, used only when the column is empty, and only after the resolved absolute path has been proved to be inside the uploads root. `{id:int}` is a route constraint, so `../`, `%2e%2e%2f` and every other traversal string fails to match the route at all and never reaches this method.

What this response deliberately does not contain, and why (M2-A07 step 3 — an over-broad `/me` becomes a personal-data endpoint by accident): `User.IsViewOnly` — not a runtime gate. At user creation it materialises a `UserRight` row per screen with `CanView` true and everything else false (`V.SMART/V.SMART.Shared/BusinessLayer/.../UserService.cs`), so its effect is already fully represented in `Rights`. Sending it too would invite a client to gate on it a second time and diverge.`User.HideManualJobOrderButton` — read only by `JobOrderService.IsManualyJobOrderHiden` for one button on one screen. It belongs to the M3 job-order endpoint, not to the bootstrap payload.`User.LevelAuthorization` — an approval-authority input, used when selecting approvers. ADR-004 §4 enforces approval authority inside the approval endpoints (module M3-4); it is not a UI gate.`User.IsProductionBased` — reaches the Blazor menu only through the QR-login path (`ShowProductionMenu = IsQrLogin && IsProductionUser`, `V.SMART/V.SMART.Shared/Layout/NavMenu.razor`). The API has no QR-login path, so on its own the flag changes nothing. Deferred until an SPA screen needs it.`UserAuthority` (12 document-type/level pairs) — deferred to M3-4. ADR-004 §4 enforces it server-side inside the approval endpoints, no M2 consumer references it, and KB-050's permission contract has no slot for it.The tenant's display name and every other `TenantInfo` member — `TenantInfo` carries a plaintext credentialed `ConnectionString` (R-01), so this endpoint projects the tenant identity from the token claim and never touches the tenant record at all. Role source (M2-A07 decision). The `ClaimTypes.Role` claim minted by `JwtTokenService`, not a fresh `User` row read: the login response (`AuthController.LoginResponse.Role`) is that same expression, so claim-sourcing keeps `/me` and `/auth/login` from disagreeing inside one token's lifetime, and it costs no query. `UserRole` has exactly two members, `Administrator` and `User`; the role the Blazor `AuthorizeView`s also name, `ERPAdmin`, does not exist in that enum (R-31) and is deliberately not propagated here. `CurrentUserService.GetUserRoleAsync()` is not called: it reads claim type `"role"` while both providers write `ClaimTypes.Role` (R-18). Failure is loud. A rights-load fault propagates out of V.SMART.Api.Authorization.IUserRightsProvider to M2-A06's handler as a `500`. It must never degrade to an empty map: an empty map renders as "no permissions" and reads to a user as a permission problem rather than an outage. The provider never negative-caches, so nothing is written on failure either.
The two GST ladders, paired by index. Read from `CommonConstants`, never retyped.
get.description:
This action is not tenant-dependent — the ladders are compile-time constants — but it
shares the group's tenant-keyed policy anyway. Carving out a per-endpoint exemption
would buy a marginal cache-entry saving in exchange for two policies to reason about,
and the failure mode of getting that wrong is a cross-tenant leak. Uniform is safer.

get.summary: Units of measure. `UnitCode` is the key; this table has no integer id.

Active terms and conditions. The active filter is the domain's — this action calls
`GetAllActiveTermsAsync` and does not re-filter, so the API cannot disagree with
the Blazor screens about what "active" means.
The screen catalogue — the permission vocabulary, not the caller's rights.
get.description: The protection decision, recorded here because it is a security decision. This returns every screen name in the tenant, which is a map of the application's surface. It is not sensitive per-user data: the same list is identical for every user in the tenant, and it discloses nothing about who may do what. The caller's own rights are a different endpoint (`GET /api/v1/me`, M2-A07) and are deliberately not merged into this one — merging them would make this response caller-dependent and force the cache key to include the user, multiplying the entry count by the user base for no benefit. It therefore requires authentication, is tenant-keyed, and is cached like the rest of the group. It projects to V.SMART.Api.Contracts.ScreenDto specifically to drop the `UserRights` navigation — returning the entity would put the tenant's entire permission matrix on the wire behind a dropdown feed.

get.summary: Currencies, as reference data for dropdowns.
get.description: Distinct from `CurrencyController`, deliberately. That controller is the CRUD surface for the Currency master — paged, sorted, filtered, writable (`/api/v1/currencies`). This is a flat, cached, read-only list for populating a selector (`/api/v1/reference/currencies`). Different lifetime, different shape, different cacheability; the route group and these summaries are what keep them distinguishable in Swagger. It excludes the `CurrencyRates` navigation — the daily rate feed changes on a different clock and is what makes the entity unsafe to cache.

A currency. Excludes `CurrencyRates` — the daily rate feed is a different concern
with a different lifetime, and it is what makes the entity unsafe to cache.

CurrencyVMPagedResult.description: The single paged-list response body for every list endpoint in this API (M2-B02). The property names are ADR-002 §2's `{ items, totalCount, pageNumber, pageSize }`verbatim; with ASP.NET Core's default camel-case JSON policy they serialise to exactlythose four names. This is one generic type, deliberately replacing thecontroller-local paged-response record pattern (the one `CurrencyController` used to declare): 60–80 structurally identicalresponse records would become 60–80 distinct interfaces in the generated TypeScriptclient (M2-B10). Why there is no `totalPages`. ADR-002 §2 names four properties and thegenerated client is frozen at M2-B03, so adding a fifth here is a contract decision, not aconvenience. It is derivable on the client from `totalCount` and `pageSize`.Note that an unrelated, unused `V.SMART.Shared.ViewModels.PagedResult`(`RejectionMasterVM.cs:33-40`) does carry `TotalPages` — it has zero referencesand is not this type. Do not confuse the two; if a file needs both namespaces it mustalias one. `TotalCount` is the count of the filtered, unpaged query — see`CurrencyService.cs:76`, where `CountAsync()` runs after the filters and before`Skip`/`Take`. Every service in `BusinessLayer/` follows that convention(INV-002); a list endpoint that reports anything else is a defect.

id.description: The stored file's identifier — the `{id}` of the download endpoint.

fileName.description: The original client file name, unmodified.

relativePath.description: Web-relative path of the stored file.

contentType.description: The content type the API resolved from the extension and will serve.

FileUploadResponse.description: The body of a successful `POST api/v1/files` (M2-B06). V.SMART.Api.Contracts.FileUploadResponse.Id is the `Correspondence.Id` the file was recorded under, and isthe only thing `GET api/v1/files/{id}` accepts. It is deliberately not a path:an identifier a caller cannot turn into a directory traversal is the strongest form of theguarantee, and it also carries tenant isolation for free, because the row lives in thetenant database resolved from the JWT. V.SMART.Api.Contracts.FileUploadResponse.RelativePath is the web-relative location on disk, in the same shape`WebFileUploadService.cs:104` returns, so a record written through the API and onewritten through Blazor are indistinguishable to every existing reader of`Correspondence.FilePath`.

GstRatesResponse.description:
The two GST ladders, paired by index: `CgstSgst[i]` is exactly half of
`Igst[i]`, because CGST and SGST each carry half the integrated rate.

totalRows.description: Data rows found in the sheet, excluding the header.

rejected.description: Rows refused, each with a reason in Errors.

errors.description: One entry per rejected row, in sheet order.

ImportResult.description:
The body of a `POST api/v1/{resource}/import` (M2-B06). An import is not a
success/failure: it is a per-row report, because a spreadsheet with one bad row must not
discard the other 499 and must not silently accept them either.

row.description: 1-based row number as it appears in the spreadsheet, header included.

ImportRowError.description:
One rejected row. Message is the business service's own refusal message
verbatim where there is one (BR-SO-001), or the DataAnnotations message from the resource's
ViewModel — never a reworded API string.

MeResponse.description: `Rights` is keyed by `Screens.ScreenName` verbatim, so a client lookup is the one-step equivalent of `rights.FirstOrDefault(r => r.Screens.ScreenName == screenName)?.CanX ?? false` (`V.SMART/V.SMART.Shared/Shared/RightsHelper.cs:7-20`). Absent rows are omitted, not materialised (BR-AUTH-002). A screen the caller holds no `UserRight` row for simply has no key — the response never carries 152 all-`false` entries. The client's default for a missing key is therefore deny, matching the database and matching the `?? false` the Blazor UI has always applied. A client that defaults a missing key to "allow" is wrong, and this contract says so. No `User` flag beyond the identity is included, and no connection string, password or token ever is (R-01). See the endpoint's remarks for the per-field justification.

screenName.description:
The screen right that gates the report's data endpoint — declared
            here so a client can decide whether to even offer the report before trying it, but the
            data endpoint enforces it independently regardless of what the client does with this.

paging.description:
Always `"in-memory"` for every entry today — see the remark on
            V.SMART.Api.Reporting.ReportRegistry. Present on every row rather than assumed, so a client cannot
            mistake this for a server-paged list.

ReportCatalogueEntry.description:
The catalogue-response shape for `GET /api/v1/reports` — one row per
            registered slug. Each report's own data endpoint lives on its own controller (see
            V.SMART.Api.Controllers.ReportsController remarks); this only lists what exists.

type.description:
A short type label for the catalogue — `"string"`, `"date"`
            or `"int"`. Not a .NET type name; this is a client-facing hint, not a contract.

required.description: Whether the report can run without it.

ReportParameterDescriptor.description: One typed parameter a report slug accepts, for the catalogue response.

ScreenDto.description:
A screen in the permission catalogue. Excludes `UserRights` — see the type-level
remarks; that navigation is the tenant's entire permission matrix.

ScreenRight.description:
One screen's five booleans, named exactly as the client's `ScreenRight` interface
names them (KB-050 § Permission-based rendering). `Hidden` carries `IsHide`:
navigation is filtered on `view && !hidden`, which is the flag's actual
purpose — it is not, and must not become, a second gate.

StateDto.description: A state. `StateCode` is the key the documents store.

TermsDto.description:
An active terms-and-conditions entry. Only active rows are returned; the endpoint is
backed by `ICommonService.GetAllActiveTermsAsync()`, so the filter is the domain's,
not this layer's.

UomDto.description: A unit of measure. `UnitCode` is the key — this table has no integer id.

Bearer.description: JWT Authorization header using the Bearer scheme. Example: "Bearer {token}"

tags.name: Files
tags.description: File upload and download over HTTP (M2-B06) — the replacement for Blazor's `IBrowserFile` on the way in and `IFileOpener`'s JS interop on the way out. Over HTTP a download is a response; there is no base64-over-SignalR equivalent and no reason to want one. Screen and rights.`[RequireScreen("Correspondences")]` is the seededscreen that owns these files (`ScreenCatalogue.cs:56`; the upload UI it mirrors is`CorrespondenceUpload.razor`). Upload requires `Create`, download requires`View`, per ADR-004 / KB-105 — the rights are evaluated by the globally registered`ScreenRightAuthorizationFilter` against the tenant database, never against acompile-time list. Tenant isolation is structural, not a check. The download resolves`{id}` through `IUnitOfWork.Correspondances`, which is scoped to thetenant-resolved `ApplicationDbContext` (M2-B07). A tenant-B token therefore queriestenant B's database, where tenant A's id either does not exist or is a different row; theanswer for "not yours" and "does not exist" is the same 404, so the response never revealswhether an id exists elsewhere. The upload is not idempotent. Every POST creates a new file (the`Guid.NewGuid()` prefix guarantees a distinct name) and a new row, so a client thatretries a timed-out request creates a duplicate. A general idempotency-key mechanism is`M2-B12-03`; until it lands, clients must not retry blind.

tags.name: Me
tags.description: M2-A07 — the SPA bootstrap endpoint: who the caller is, which tenant they are in, their role, and their complete screen-rights map, in one call. PRESENTATION ONLY (ADR-004 §3). The map this endpoint returns exists so the clientcan render a permission-correct navigation and disable controls the caller cannot use. Itis never the enforcement point. The server re-checks every request independentlythrough V.SMART.Api.Authorization.ScreenRightAuthorizationFilter, and nothing here relaxes that filter.A client must not treat this response as authoritative. Route (M2-A07 decision, for M2-B01). This ships at `/api/v1/me` — the nameADR-004 §3, KB-105 and KB-080 §9 all use, and the name M2-C02 will code against — making itthe first versioned route in an API whose other routes are still `api/auth` and`api/currencies`. The version segment is a literal here because the versioningmechanism does not exist yet. When M2-B01 lands it must re-express this route through theversioning convention without changing the URL; the URL is the contract, the literalis not. Thin controller (ADR-002 §2). Read claims, one provider call, map, return. Nobusiness logic, no database access of its own: every value in the response comes eitherfrom the caller's own token or from V.SMART.Api.Authorization.IUserRightsProvider.

tags.name: Purchase Order
tags.description:
M2-B08 print-only stub. This is not the Purchase Order resource controller — no CRUD
exists here; a future module-wave task (M3/M4) that builds one is expected to fold this
action in, at the same route, and delete this file. Placed on its own resource-shaped
controller rather than a shared print controller because V.SMART.Api.Authorization.RequireScreenAttribute
is class-level only (KB-105 §2.2) and this route needs a different screen than the other
two seeded print entries.

tags.name: Reference
tags.description: M2-B09 — the small, slow-changing lookup lists every screen needs before it can render a dropdown, behind one cached route group. Closes KB-041 item B6 and the reference-data half of C1. Every action is a single `ICommonService` call plus a projection. Noquery is written against `ApplicationDbContext` here and no business logic liveshere (ADR-002 §2). The one action that is not a service call — `gst-rates` — readsthe domain's own constants rather than restating them. Why `[NoScreenRight]` and not `[RequireScreen]`. Reference data iswhat a screen needs in order to render at all; there is no single screen that owns"the list of states". Gating it on a screen right would deadlock the UI for exactly thereason KB-105 §2.4 gives for `GET /api/v1/me` — a user must be able to fetch thevocabulary before the app can decide what to show them. The endpoints still requireauthentication and are still tenant-scoped; this is an explicit, greppable opt-out fromthe screen-right axis, not from authorization.

tags.name: Salary
tags.description:
M2-B08 print-only stub. Deliberately the entry that exercises
V.SMART.Api.Reporting.PrintGenerator.GenerateSalarySlipReport rather than
`ReportService.Generate_Report` — proving the registry's second generator branch,
not just the dominant one. See V.SMART.Api.Controllers.PurchaseOrdersController's remarks for why
this is its own controller.
